newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia c bank may help troubled Natskredit bank.
newsitem.headline: Russia c bank may help troubled Natskredit bank.

text.p: Russia's central bank would consider a programme to restore the liquidity of Bank Natsionalny Kredit (Natskredit) if the troubled bank proposes the idea, a central bank spokesman said on Thursday.

"We stick to the logic that there should be an initiative either from the board or from the owners," Alexei Sitnin told Reuters. "There should be a well-considered wish on their part, supported by real actions. If that happens, why should we not help the bank stand on its feet?"
Sitnin said central bank help would mean stricter control over the bank.

"A stabilisation credit follows a detailed analysis of the financial situation at a bank. That's why if a bank applies for a stabilisation credit, we either impose a temporary administration there or set up a group to study its financial situation," he said.
Natsionalny Kredit was unavailable for comment on Thursday.
In March, the bank's management applied to the State Duma lower house of parliament for help in receiving a special credit of $70 million from the central bank.
The Kommersant Daily newspaper reported on Thursday that Natskredit was not seeking a central bank stabilisation credit.
It said the bank wanted to attract investors, possibly by selling some of its stock to a foreign partner.

Last summer, just before a liquidity crisis shook Moscow banks, some big Russian banks closed credit lines to Natsionalny Kredit after the bank failed to make payments on time, dealers said. At the time, it was Russia's 17th biggest bank.
Subsequently, Natsionalny Kredit cut back some of its activities and sold some of its branches. And since then, its management has been trying to restructure the bank.

Many small- and medium-sized undercapitalised Russian banks still face difficulties, and the central bank withdraws licences from several banks every week. It has also imposed temporary administration on several banks.
